about: The rights register (CONTEXT.md; PLAN 6 and 6.1; ADR 0006, ADR 0020): one row per Origin and per intermediary Channel, with the terms read, a proposal, and Alex's decision. This file is the single table. docs/v2/rights-register.md and packages/core/src/rights-register.generated.ts are generated from it (npm run gen); atlas/rights.py reads it. A row permits something on a public Surface only when its decision is signed by Alex. The builder proposes and never fills in a decision.

rows.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics
rows.used_for: CPI, payrolls, unemployment, participation, wages. v2.0 (M7, M13).

capture.note: CPI-U all items (not adjusted and seasonally adjusted), the unemployment rate and total nonfarm payrolls, monthly, for the thirty years ending this year: three requests without a key, ten years each.

Labor force participation, core CPI, rent of primary residence, average hourly earnings of production workers and the average price of eggs (monthly); the labor share index and real median weekly earnings (quarterly). The thirty years ending this year: three requests without a key. Every one of the seven began before 1997 (checked 2026-11-11), so no year of the window is before a series began.

quotes: everything that we publish, both in hard copy and electronically, is in the public domain, except for previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations
You are free to use our public domain material without specific permission
we do ask that you cite the Bureau of Labor Statistics as the source

terms.note: The site refused the automated request (HTTP 403).

rows.attribution: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

proposal.note: Public domain by the Bureau's own statement. Cite the Bureau on every figure and download.

open_questions: The API terms of service and the API FAQ were not read: bls.gov refused the automated request for both (HTTP 403, 2026-11-11). Read them before signing.

Limits without a key, as far as M7 and M13 could check them on 2026-11-11 by asking the API: a request for more than ten years is cut to ten years from its start year, with a message; an unknown series is left out, with a message; a year with no figure yet (this year, each January) is answered "No Data Available for Series ... Year: ...". The capture job asks for thirty years in three requests per endpoint, accepts only that last message and only of the current year, and treats any other message as an incomplete answer. The daily limit on requests without a key is believed to be 25 and was not confirmed from the page; the job makes six requests per run, two runs a day.

rows.name: Bureau of Economic Analysis
rows.used_for: GDP, PCE, income, profits, trade balance. v2.0 (M15): six requests a run, with a free API key (BEA_API_KEY) kept outside the repository.

datasets: National Income and Product Accounts, Table 1.1.1
capture.note: Table 1.1.1, percent change from the preceding period in real gross domestic product, quarterly, every year and every line in one request (about 2.0 MB on 2026-11-11). Line 1 is read.

datasets: National Income and Product Accounts, Table 1.1.5
capture.note: Table 1.1.5, gross domestic product in current dollars, quarterly, every year and every line in one request (about 1.9 MB on 2026-11-11). Line 1 is read. The API gives the figures in millions of dollars (UNIT_MULT 6) though the table's note says billions; the multiplier is pinned.

datasets: National Income and Product Accounts, Table 1.1.6
capture.note: Table 1.1.6, real gross domestic product in chained dollars, quarterly, every year and every line in one request (about 1.1 MB on 2026-11-11). Line 1 is read, in millions of chained (2017) dollars. The reference year is pinned as a text the table's note must hold: a rebase keeps the capture from being whole until the pin and the Series are changed.

datasets: National Income and Product Accounts, Table 1.12
capture.note: Table 1.12, national income by type of income, quarterly, every year and every line in one request (about 3.7 MB on 2026-11-11). Line 45 is read: corporate profits after tax without inventory valuation and capital consumption adjustments. Profits are published a release later than GDP, so the line ends a quarter earlier than the table.

datasets: National Income and Product Accounts, Table 2.6
capture.note: Table 2.6, personal income and its disposition, monthly, every year and every line in one request (about 8.6 MB on 2026-11-11, 0.3 MB compressed). Four lines are read: personal income, personal consumption expenditures, the personal saving rate and real disposable personal income.

International Transactions Accounts: the balance on goods and services, all countries, quarterly, seasonally adjusted, every year in one request (about 0.1 MB on 2026-11-11). Quarterly rates, not annualized. The API has no monthly frequency for these accounts; the monthly balance of the FT-900 release is not in it.

quotes: Citations are appreciated and appropriate.

terms.note: The sign-up form asks for agreement to published terms of service; the terms document itself was not read.

rows.attribution: Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.

proposal.note: U.S. federal works are not subject to copyright in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105). That is the basis proposed here; the pages read do not themselves state a licence. Cite the Bureau.

open_questions: The API terms of service were not read: the sign-up page asks for agreement to them and M15 did not fetch the document. Read them before signing, and record any required notice here.

Request limits, as the API's user guide gives them and M15 did not test: 100 requests a minute, 100 MB a minute, 30 errors a minute, and an hour's lock-out (HTTP 429) beyond them. The capture job makes six requests a run, about 17 MB, two runs a day.

The API repeats the key it was asked with in every answer. The capture kit replaces every copy before anything is kept, so the bytes kept are the answer with that one change (ADR 0029). Confirm that keeping them so is acceptable.

The monthly trade balance v1 showed is the FT-900 release, compiled with the Census Bureau, and is not in this API. The quarterly balance from the International Transactions Accounts is captured here under a new key; the monthly figure waits for the Census files (M16).

rows.name: Federal Reserve Board
origins: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
rows.used_for: H.15 rates, H.10 exchange rates, H.4.1 balance sheet, Z.1 net worth, through the Data Download Program. v2.0 (M13).

capture.note: Treasury constant-maturity yields, business daily since 1962, the Data Download Program's own H.15 package, whole history on each run (about 1 MB on 2026-11-11).
The H.15 package of monthly averages (30 series since 1934, about 115 KB on 2026-11-11), read for the federal funds effective rate.

The H.10 package of daily exchange rates (23 currencies since 1971). The whole history is about 2.6 MB and the program answers it with an empty body, so it is asked for in three spans (0.6, 0.9 and 0.8 MB on 2026-11-11).

The H.10 package of daily dollar indexes since 2006 (about 0.2 MB on 2026-11-11), read for the nominal broad index. The program labels the unit "Index:_1997_Jan_100"; the figures are on the base January 2006 = 100 (the mean of January 2006 is 100.0).

Table 5 of the H.4.1 release, the consolidated statement of condition of all Federal Reserve Banks: 128 series of Wednesday levels since December 2002 (about 0.8 MB on 2026-11-11), read for total assets.

datasets: Z.1 Financial Accounts of the United States
capture.note: The Z.1 package S1M.b (Q), the balance sheet of households and nonprofit organizations, quarterly since 1945 (about 0.13 MB on 2026-11-11), read for net worth.

datasets: G.17 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization
capture.note: The G.17 package of the major industrial production and capacity utilization aggregates, monthly since 1919 (about 80 KB on 2026-11-11), read for the total index.
The G.19 package of consumer credit outstanding, seasonally adjusted, monthly since 1943 (about 75 KB on 2026-11-11), read for the total.
The H.6 package of monthly money stock measures in billions, since 1959 (about 0.14 MB on 2026-11-11), read for M2, seasonally adjusted.

datasets: Charge-Off and Delinquency Rates on Loans and Leases at Commercial Banks
capture.note: The package of delinquency rates at all commercial banks, quarterly since 1985 (about 23 KB on 2026-11-11), read for credit card loans, seasonally adjusted.

quotes: Unless otherwise indicated, information on Board's website is in the public domain and may be copied and distributed without permission.
Please cite to the Board as the source of the information.

rows.attribution: Source: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.

proposal.note: Public domain by the Board's own statement, unless a release says otherwise. Cite the Board.

open_questions: Some releases carry data the Board marks as coming from a non-Board source. Checked in M13 (2026-11-11) for each series read under this row: the label rows of the downloaded files carry no source mark for any of them. Two things for Alex to weigh before signing: the H.15 Treasury constant-maturity yields are the U.S. Treasury's figures and the federal funds effective rate is calculated by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, both published by the Board in H.15; the H.10 exchange rates are noon buying rates in New York collected by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. None is a private vendor's series. The H.15 package also holds commercial paper and bank prime rates, which are captured in the file and not read into any Series.

rows.name: International Monetary Fund
rows.used_for: Japan CPI fix; G20 CPI and exchange rates (SDMX 3.0), v2.0 (M14): two requests a run. Later WEO GDP and commodity prices, v2.2.

capture.note: The all-items consumer price index of the nineteen G20 countries, monthly, whole history in one request (about 0.6 MB on 2026-11-11). The reference period of each index is pinned as the Fund labelled it that day: a rebase keeps the capture from being whole until the pin and the Series are changed. The adapter reads a value as observed (the Fund's derivation codes O and R), an estimate (SE, SEME, SEHI) or projected (SP); on 2026-11-11 every value here was O. One value under any other code, or under none, keeps the whole answer from being whole.

National currency per U.S. dollar, monthly period average, for the fifteen G20 countries outside the euro area that are not the United States, and for the euro area (the Fund's G163), whole history in one request (about 0.4 MB on 2026-11-11). The mark T sat on 39 Observations that day, at changes of exchange-rate regime and redenominations; the dataflow's structure gives it no meaning, so it is carried as a footnote and read as nothing.

quotes: Distributed or reproduced Data must appear accurately with attribution to the IMF as the source.
Users shall not infringe upon the integrity of the Data
terms.note: As summarised from the page: data may be downloaded, copied, published and distributed with attribution; commercial reuse needs permission; automated bulk downloading needs explicit permission; use to train large language models needs explicit permission.

rows.attribution: Source: International Monetary Fund.

proposal.note: Allow display, download and storage with attribution, for a non-commercial site. Do not describe as usable for model training: the terms as summarised reserve that.

open_questions: Does a daily request to the SDMX API count as automated bulk downloading, which the terms as summarised reserve? What M14 would ask for is two requests a run (35 series, about 1.1 MB, whole history each time). That is a fact about the job, not an answer: confirm with the page or with the Fund before the row is signed for storage.
The wording was read through a tool that returns short extracts. Open the page before signing (PLAN 6: IMF reuse wording still unverified).

The Fund republishes national figures. The CPI Observations read here are all marked 'reported official data' and the exchange rates 'raw data'; whether a national statistics office's own terms add anything for its index is not looked into.
